brief.gloss: The set of instructions and facts a client or employer gives you for a piece of writing.

copy.gloss: Writing whose purpose is to sell or persuade people to act.

seo.gloss: Search engine optimisation: writing so that search engines such as Google find your page.

portfolio.gloss: A collection of your best work that shows employers and clients what you can do.

content writing.gloss: Writing that informs and educates the reader.

copywriting.gloss: Writing that persuades the reader to buy, sign up or act.

capstone.gloss: The final project of the course, where you write ten pieces for one business.

template.gloss: A ready-made outline in the editor, with headings that divide the piece into parts.

reading grade.gloss: An estimate of how hard a text is to read; a lower number means easier reading.

features into benefits.gloss: Saying what a product does for the reader, not only what it has.

call to action.gloss: A sentence that tells the reader what to do next, usually starting with a verb such as "Order".

conversion.gloss: A reader who takes the action the copy asks for, such as buying or signing up.

editing in passes.gloss: Improving a draft in several readings: big things first, then sentences, then details.

7 cs of communication.gloss: Seven qualities of effective writing: clear, concise, concrete, correct, coherent, complete, courteous.

key message.gloss: The one sentence the reader must remember if they forget everything else.

jargon.gloss: Special words that only experts know.

freelancer.gloss: A self-employed writer who works for several clients.

seo writer.gloss: A writer who creates content that appears high in search engine results.

technical writer.gloss: A writer of manuals, documentation and standard operating procedures.

ux writer.gloss: A writer of the words inside apps and websites.

ghostwriter.gloss: A writer who writes books, speeches or posts in someone else's name.
